stories.title: Dell Extends AI Data Platform with Unified Semantic Layer, Enterprise Knowledge Graph, and Knowledge Agents
stories.body: On October 6, 2026, Dell extended its Data Orchestration Engine with three new capabilities: a Unified Semantic Layer, an Enterprise Knowledge Graph, and Knowledge Agents, positioning the stack as the connective layer between enterprise data and production AI. Dell also added a new capability in its Data Processing Engine designed to accelerate enterprise data preparation for AI workloads. The move is a direct vendor commitment that agents require a grounded knowledge layer — not raw data — before they can function reliably at enterprise scale.
stories.why: This is proof-of-architecture from a major infrastructure vendor: enterprises need a semantic and graph layer before agents ship, which is exactly the data-foundation argument Graas makes on every discovery call. When a prospect's IT team says 'we'll just connect the agent to our data warehouse,' this Dell launch illustrates why that is insufficient and what the right stack actually looks like.

stories.title: Sierra Partners with Stripe to Enable End-to-End Payments Inside AI Agent Calls, Launches Personal Agent Protocol with Meta and Walmart
stories.body: On October 20, 2026, Sierra announced a partnership with Stripe allowing customers to converse with a Sierra AI agent, pay, and receive a receipt on the same call — with healthcare payments company Cedar named as an early adopter. Separately, Sierra disclosed it is co-building the Personal Agent Protocol alongside Meta, Genesys, Shopify, Stripe, and Walmart, an open standard defining how personal agents interact with businesses including how payments work when an agent acts on a consumer's behalf. Sierra said it will publish the v0.1 specification later in October 2026.
stories.why: Sierra — a direct competitor and frequent name on retail RFPs — is moving fast to own the transaction layer of agentic commerce, not just the conversation layer. A retailer evaluating 'conversation AI' vendors needs to understand Sierra is pitching an end-to-end agent OS with embedded payments; Graas sellers should be ready to position against that full-stack ambition and show where Graas's context and data layer is differentiated.

stories.title: Gartner 2026 Hype Cycle: Agentic AI at Peak of Inflated Expectations — Only 17% of Enterprises Live, 40%+ of Projects Forecast to Be Cancelled by 2027
stories.body: Gartner's 2026 Hype Cycle for Artificial Intelligence, published October 1, 2026, places agentic AI at the Peak of Inflated Expectations and finds only 17% of organizations have deployed AI agents, while more than 60% plan to do so within two years. Gartner predicts over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by end of 2027 due to escalating costs, unclear business value, and inadequate risk controls — not model failure. The report explicitly names 'agent washing' — vendors relabeling chatbots and RPA as agents — as a core hype-cycle symptom, estimating only roughly 130 of thousands of vendors claiming agentic capability are genuine.
stories.why: This Gartner report is the single best objection-handling asset for stalled-pilot conversations: when a retail CIO says 'we tried agents and it didn't work,' the data shows governance and data-foundation gaps — not technology — are what kill projects. Graas can use the 40% cancellation forecast to frame its context-layer and pre-built retail ontology as the infrastructure that separates the 17% in production from the 83% still stuck.

stories.title: McKinsey State of AI 2026: 32% of Enterprises Skipped a Software Purchase to Build In-House — But Enterprise EBIT Impact Stays Flat at 37%
stories.body: McKinsey's State of AI: Global Survey 2026, published August 25, 2026, and drawing on 1,719 respondents across 97 countries, found that nearly a third of organizations (32%) decided against buying at least one software product or feature because agentic coding tools made an in-house build feasible — a figure that rises to nearly half among McKinsey's 'AI high performers.' At the same time, the share of organizations reporting any enterprise EBIT impact from AI remained flat at 37%, unchanged from 2025, and one in five organizations said AI operating costs are beginning to constrain deployment. Large enterprises scaling AI agents rose from 27% to 40% year-over-year.
stories.why: The build-vs-buy shift is live inside every retail and CPG IT budget conversation right now, and the flat EBIT number is the counter-argument Graas needs at hand: building in-house is not translating into bottom-line results. This lets sellers reframe 'we'll build it ourselves' as a risk, not a saving, and position Graas's pre-built retail-domain context layer as the faster, lower-TCO path to production outcomes.

stories.title: BCG: GenAI-Enabled Supply Chain Agents Deliver +2–4% In-Stock Rate and 40–60% Admin Savings for Global CPG Leader
stories.body: A BCG May 2026 executive perspectives report documents a global CPG manufacturer that deployed GenAI-enabled agents to shift replenishment from reactive to proactive, generating in-stock alerts and smart replenishment recommendations — including DC-to-store transfers and expedited orders — validated through a human-in-the-loop workflow. Measured outcomes include a 2–4 percentage point improvement in in-stock rate driving revenue lift, a 4–10 percentage point improvement in fill rate, and 40–60% administrative savings for the planning team. The deployment was built on a modular agent back-end designed for future expansion across additional retailer collaboration workflows.
stories.why: This is a named-outcome proof point in the exact workflow — supply chain ordering and replenishment — that Graas sells into. The human-in-the-loop validation model and modular back-end architecture directly mirror what Graas proposes; sellers can use this BCG case to validate the category with skeptical CPG buyers who are still treating AI as an experiment rather than a production system.
